Once the settlement is paid, the employee can view and download the same statement in the Employee Portal My payslips , while their portal access lasts. That access normally ends on the payment date, so extend it in Employee Master if they need longer. What happens in the books Approval posts one settlement journal dated the leaving date. It clears the amounts used from gratuity, leave salary and other provisions, posts the difference to expense, takes back any lapsed accrual provision, reduces loan receivables, and posts net due to Salaries Payable or Recoverable from employees. Payment is separate and clears the payable through cash/bank. Once it is paid, the leaver's ERP and Employee Portal access ends on the payment date or the last working day, if later ; without a payment it ends 30 days after the last working day. Reversing the payment brings the 30 days back. A negative net is not paid out; it is recorded as an employee receivable. Rights PAYROLLFS access controls viewing; draft prepares and submits; configured approvers decide; post controls reversal; pay controls payment and payment reversal. Payroll Setup write is required to correct setup accounts. Company access and employee sensitive rights apply. Questions and mistakes Employee is not available: status must be On notice or Left, and the leaving date must be entered. Cannot submit yet: wait until the leaving date, decide/delete leave through that date, and resolve every salary month. A month left to its run must have a posted run with the employee; a month paid here cannot have a run beyond Draft. Salary month appears in both workflows: choose whether the run or settlement pays it. A submitted settlement later causes the payroll run to require recalculation and exclude that employee/month. Leave or gratuity amount is unexpected: check approved and pending leave through the exit date, unpaid day treatment, current compensation, grade/leave rules, company daily rate method, and provision setup. Override is refused: provide a non negative amount and a reason. Keep supporting approval evidence with the settlement. No GL account/cost center: configure the relevant payroll/provision/loan account and employee cost center before submission. Settlement is payable through Interim Payroll: a posted positive net settlement can be included in one Interim Payroll batch; do not also mark it paid directly. Cannot reverse: reverse the payment first and remove the settlement from any Interim Payroll batch. Reversal requires a reason. Related pages Employee Master employees.html · Employee Change employee change.html · Payroll Setup payroll setup.html · Payroll Run payroll run.html · Interim Payroll payroll interim.html · Provisions provisions.html

pages.title: Provisions
pages.summary: Maintain leave, gratuity and other provisions so payroll and year-end reporting stay aligned.
pages.text: Provisions What it is for Payroll provisions track employee liabilities that accrue over time, including end of service gratuity, unused leave salary, and company defined accruals such as travel or education benefits. Rules are configured in Payroll Setup; monthly provision amounts are calculated with Payroll Run and posted when that run is posted. The Provisions screen has Statement , Claims , and Openings tabs. The setup formulas and accounts are maintained separately in Payroll Setup → Provisions. Before you start HR/Finance have agreed the policy for gratuity, leave salary, and each additional accrual. Payroll Setup → Provisions has the applicable formula, grade rules, employee exceptions, and active expense/liability accounts. Opening provision balances already in the GL have been imported with their as of dates through Master Data Import; do not enter them again as a new GL posting. Employee grade, joining date, compensation, leave balances, and cost center are current. Step by step Configure the policy 1. In Payroll Setup → Provisions, select the company and configure gratuity: Basic or Gross base, day rate rule, minimum service, cap, start point, service slabs, and expense/provision accounts. 2. Configure leave salary on Basic or Gross and set its expense/liability accounts. Its days come from the employee's available balance plus booked days for leave types that use balances. 3. Define other accrual types with a unique code and either a fixed annual amount or a percentage of Basic/Gross. Add non overlapping grade level rules, company specific account overrides, and any employee specific value or exclusion. Decide whether the balance is paid at leaving or lapses. 4. Verify account types and company ownership. The expense account must be an active postable Expense; the provision account an active postable Liability. Review balances and claims 1. In Statement , select the company and month range. Filter by provision or employee, then select an employee/provision row to inspect dated movements and linked documents/journals. The report also compares closing provision amounts with the GL accounts where available; investigate any difference. 2. In Claims , record an accrual claim when the company pays an eligible benefit, such as an approved education or travel cost. Select employee, accrual type, payment date, amount, cash/bank account, and note; retain supporting evidence. 3. Review the claim's journal and updated balance. If entered incorrectly, reverse it with a reason rather than editing its posted record. 4. In Openings , maintain an employee's provision amount as of a date when loading an existing balance already represented in the GL. This is a balance brought forward, not a new journal. For many employees, use Master Data Import → Opening Provisions. 5. At termination, review the provision amounts in Final Settlement. The settlement pays configured balances at leaving or takes back balances that lapse. What happens in the books Payroll Setup does not post. Each posted payroll run debits provision expense by employee cost center and credits the provision liability for the month's movement; a changed calculation can adjust an already provided balance. A claim debits the relevant provision liability and credits cash/bank. Final Settlement consumes the provision and posts any difference to expense; accruals configured to lapse are taken back. Opening balances imported from an existing GL are balance records only and are not posted again. Rights Payroll Setup access/write controls provision configuration. PAYROLL access controls provision balance review; PAYROLL pay controls accrual claims and reversals. Final Settlement permissions control the exit payout/clearance workflow. Company access applies. Questions and mistakes No provision movement in the run: verify the policy is enabled, the employee is included in the run, relevant grade/employee rules cover them, and both accounts are valid. Accrual amount is zero or unexpected: inspect the fixed annual amount/percentage, Basic/Gross selection, grade range, employee exception, service dates, and effective employee pay. Leave salary differs from the leave report: compare leave types that use a balance, employee entitlement overrides, approved/booked days, the as of date, and the daily rate method. Provision account rejected: expense must be an active postable Expense and provision must be an active postable Liability; company overrides must belong to that company. Opening balance doubles the liability: confirm the opening balance was imported as an as of balance already represented in the GL, not posted as a new expense/liability journal. Claim exceeds the expected balance: review prior posted runs, opening balance date, earlier claims/payouts, and whether a final settlement has taken control of the employee's provisions. Cannot make a claim or change a balance: check the Payroll pay right, company access, and whether a final settlement is beyond Draft. Final Settlement amount differs from monthly provision: the settlement recalculates on the leaving date and clears the liability actually provided; the difference is posted to expense or taken back. Related pages Payroll Setup payroll setup.html · Payroll Run payroll run.html · Final Settlement payroll final settlement.html · Master Data Import master import.html

pages.title: Employee Requests
pages.summary: Manage employee queries, claims and requests from the portal or the ERP’s request workflows.
pages.text: Employee Requests What it is for Employee Requests is the ERP side work queue for requests submitted through Employee Self Service. It brings employee queries and cases to the relevant handler, while claims and other request types continue through their own approval and payroll/accounting workflows. Requests may include a question or case, reimbursement claim, loan/advance request, payroll query, or a leave request that is initiated and tracked through the portal. Besides these, HR can set up request types of its own a salary certificate, IT support, a company car … , each with its own form; see Request types request types . This screen is for managing the request and its communication; it is not a substitute for the Payroll Loan, Leave, or payroll posting documents. Before you start The employee record is current, with company and line manager where the request type requires them. Employee portal access is enabled for the employee and the relevant roles have access to Employee Requests. The portal categories and policies are configured: reimbursement categories/pay elements, loan limits/types, and approval rules where used. The handler knows which actions belong in Employee Requests and which require the linked operational module. Step by step 1. Open Employee Requests and filter the list by company, request type, or status to find new and open work. 2. Open the request. Confirm the employee, category, submitted details, internal notes, and any supporting files before acting. 3. Add internal notes for the HR/payroll team. Keep notes factual and do not put sensitive payroll or identity details in a case that is visible to users who should not see them. 4. For a query, respond or route it to the appropriate handler and close it when resolved. The employee can also close their own query from the portal at any time while it is open: Mark resolved with an optional note, shown as the outcome or Withdraw a reason is required . Either shows in the query's history; a query the employee marked resolved can still be reopened within 14 days. Loan, advance and claim requests are unchanged. 5. For a reimbursement, use the configured manager and approval flow. If approved, its category specific earning is carried into the relevant month in Earnings and Deductions and paid with payroll; the claim itself is not a bank payment. 6. For a loan/advance request, check the configured loan type and limits, then follow the approval and payout workflow in Loans and Advances payroll loan.html . 7. For leave, use the Leave Register and approval workflow for the authoritative dates, balance, and return handling. 8. Reopen or follow up requests that need more information; close only after the business action is complete and the employee has a clear resolution. Request types The Types tab it needs the setup right lists the requests employees can raise from the portal's Requests → Other , besides payroll queries, loans and claims. For each type: Name and description: what the employee sees, e.g. Salary certificate: for a bank or an embassy . A name can't repeat a portal request of its own Overtime, Loan … . Fields: the type's form, up to 20: short or long text, a number, a date, a choice two options or more , yes/no, or files. Tick Required for the ones the employee must fill. Goes to: its handler directly, or the employee's line manager first , who approves or rejects it in the portal's Team; once approved, it goes on to the handler. An employee with no line manager goes straight to the handler. Each type is a category in the Handlers tab, by its name, so set who handles it there. Answer within: an optional number of days, counted from the day it reaches the handler. The request shows Answer by with the date, and after it overdue , in the list and on Home. It is a reminder, not a block. The answer is a document: for a certificate. The request can be resolved only once HR has attached the document under Supporting documents; the employee downloads it from the portal. Companies: none means every company; otherwise only the employees of the companies chosen see it. Active: untick to stop new requests of a type; the ones already raised carry on. Requests of a type are numbered from one series, RQ 2026 0001 see Numbering numbering.html . They are handled like a query: reply, internal notes, files, Resolve with what was done, Reject with the reason, reassign. The employee can withdraw one, giving a reason, while it is open, and reopen it within 14 days of it being resolved. Example HR sets up Salary certificate : fields Addressed to required and Purpose a choice: Bank loan, Visa, Other , to the line manager first, answered within 3 days, the answer a document. An employee asks for one addressed to Example Bank ; their manager approves it in Team; it reaches HR, due in 3 days. HR attaches the certificate and resolves it, and the employee downloads it from the request. What happens in the books Employee Requests itself is a workflow record and does not post to the general ledger. An approved reimbursement can become an earning input for Payroll; a loan request can become a loan document; a leave request can become a Leave Register document. Those downstream modules perform their own approvals, postings, and payment records. Rights Employee Requests access and handler rights are configured separately from portal access. The line manager, assigned handler, HR, and payroll staff should receive only the rights needed for their work. Access to employee sensitive pay/bank information remains controlled by Employees sensitive rights and the respective payroll module permissions. Questions and mistakes No requests appear: check the employee's portal access, company access, request handler rights, and whether the correct status/type filter is selected. Manager does not receive the task: verify the manager link on Employee Master and the request type's approval configuration. Reimbursement is approved but not paid: check the assigned payroll month, its Earnings and Deductions entry, and whether that month's run has been calculated and posted. Loan request is approved but not paid: approval is not payout; prepare the loan payout or Interim Payroll payment using its own workflow. Leave request and register disagree: update or decide the leave in Leave Register; the case thread is not the authoritative leave record. A type does not show in the portal: check it is active and for the employee's company. Resolve is refused for a certificate: attach the document under Supporting documents first. A request of a type is not on Home yet: it is still with the line manager; it comes to the handler once approved. File or note is missing: reopen the request and inspect its attachment list and history; do not recreate a duplicate request unless the employee must resubmit. Related pages Employee Master employees.html · Payroll Setup payroll setup.html · Loans and Advances payroll loan.html · Leave leave.html · Payroll Run payroll run.html

pages.title: Clearances
pages.summary: A leaver's clearance, step by step (Finance, IT, HR …), before the final settlement goes for approval.
pages.text: Clearances What it is for Before an employee leaves, each department clears them: Finance checks loans and advances, IT collects the laptop and closes the accounts, HR takes back the documents. Clearances tracks those steps for every employee on notice or who has left, until their final settlement is posted. The final settlement payroll final settlement.html can't be submitted for approval until every step is signed off. Before you start Set up needs the Clearances setup right : open Clearances, choose the company and select Set up . The steps, in the order they run. Each has its name, its team the users who sign it off; they need Clearances access and its checklist, one item a line. Whether the steps run in order IT opens once Finance has signed or all at once . The deduction pay element an amount to recover posts through for example "Assets not returned" , if steps may enter one. A company with no set up of its own uses Finance → IT → HR, with a short checklist each. Saving no steps at all switches clearance off for the company: its settlements then don't wait for one. A change to the set up applies to clearances started from then on. Step by step A clearance starts When an employee is put On notice or marked Left with a leaving date in Employees employees.html , their clearance starts with the company's steps. It also starts for a leaver whose final settlement is not yet posted, the first time anyone opens Clearances. If the employee becomes Active again before anyone signed, the clearance goes. Sign off a step 1. The step's team sees it on Home under Clearances Waiting for You , or opens Clearances Waiting for my team . 2. Open the employee. Tick each item done, and write any notes. 3. If something wasn't returned, enter the amount to recover and what it is for. For example, 1,500.00 for "laptop not returned". 4. Save keeps your work; Sign off completes the step. In order, the next step then opens for its team. A step with no team is signed off by users with the Clearances manage right, who may also sign off any step. Reopen manage takes a signed step back, with a reason, until the final settlement is posted. The final settlement Once every step is signed off, the clearance is Complete and the final settlement can be submitted. Each amount to recover is already on it as a deduction line "Clearance: IT" , which HR can change there with a reason. What the employee sees In the Employee Portal, the leaver's Home shows Your clearance before leaving : each step done, in progress or waiting and what is still open in it for example "Laptop returned" . They never see the notes or the amounts. Rights access sees the company's clearances and lets a team member sign off their own step; manage signs off any step and reopens; setup sets the steps. Related pages Final Settlements payroll final settlement.html Employees employees.html

pages.title: Fixed Asset Configuration
pages.summary: Configure the fixed asset classes, accounts and defaults used when assets are added and depreciated.
pages.text: Fixed Asset Configuration What it is for Fixed Asset Configuration has three tabs: Settings , Account Determination , and Asset Classes . Together they determine where acquisitions first post, which accounts each asset class uses, and the default valuation/depreciation rules for new assets. Before you start Fixed Asset Clearing, cost, accumulated depreciation, expense, and any work in progress accounts are agreed with Finance. Active postable accounts exist in the Chart of Accounts with the correct type and company/shared scope. Finance has agreed the asset kinds, useful lives, depreciation methods, residual value, and account assignment. Step by step Settings tab Select a company and set its Fixed Asset Clearing Account . Asset purchases entered through supported finance/procurement documents first accumulate here; Asset Capitalization later transfers the amount to the asset's cost account. The clearing account must be an active postable Asset or Liability account, not cash/bank, a party control account, or an account already controlled by Fixed Assets. Account Determination tab Create a coded determination, then select its Shared row or a specific company row. Map the accounts displayed for the asset functions, such as asset cost, accumulated depreciation, depreciation expense, clearing, and work in progress. A blank company field falls back to the shared row. The class points to a determination; accounts are not entered separately on each asset. Check every account's type, active/postable status, and company ownership. Asset controlled accounts cannot be used as cash/bank or in incompatible roles. Asset Classes tab Create a class and choose its kind: Tangible, Intangible, Land, or Assets under Construction AuC . For depreciable Tangible/Intangible classes, set the default Straight Line or Written Down Value method, useful life, WDV rate when applicable, and residual percentage. Select an account determination and choose whether the class is shared or company specific. Land and AuC are not depreciated by the ordinary scheduled run. AuC is used for accumulation and later settlement into completed assets. Test one representative asset and acquisition/capitalization flow before using a class operationally. What happens in the books Configuration saves no journal. The clearing account is used by acquisition postings, account determinations are used by capitalization/depreciation/retirement postings, and asset classes provide defaults to asset records. Changing an account mapping does not rewrite previously posted journals. Rights FACONFIG access allows viewing; write allows changing settings, determinations, and classes. Restrict write access to Fixed Asset/Finance setup owners. Questions and mistakes Purchase cannot use the clearing account: use a postable Asset or Liability account for the correct company; do not choose cash/bank, a vendor/customer control account, or an asset controlled account. Company account is rejected in Shared: shared rows need shared accounts. Put a company owned account in that company's override row. Class cannot be selected: check that it is Active, is shared or belongs to the selected company, and points to an active account determination. Class kind or company cannot be changed: once assets use the class, its kind and company scope are protected. Depreciation does not post: verify the class's determination contains the expense and accumulated depreciation accounts, and the asset has a cost center. Related pages Fixed Asset Master fixed asset master.html · Capitalization fixed asset capitalization.html · Depreciation Run depreciation run.html · Capital Work in Progress capital work in progress.html

pages.title: Fixed Asset Master
pages.summary: Maintain the asset record that contains its details, class, location and book value basis.
pages.text: Fixed Asset Master What it is for Fixed Asset Master holds the asset's descriptive, assignment, and book information. Its list lets you search/filter the asset population; opening an asset provides Details and History tabs. Transactions such as capitalization, depreciation, transfer, and retirement remain in their own modules and appear in this asset's history. Before you start Fixed Asset Configuration fixed asset config.html has an active class and account determination for the company. The asset's company, class, description, acquisition facts, cost center, and depreciation defaults are known. Determine whether this is a Planned asset awaiting acquisition/capitalization or an already capitalized asset being reviewed. Step by step Find or create an asset Use the list filters for company, class, status, or search terms such as asset number, description, serial number, or tag/barcode. Select New Asset to create a Planned record; the system assigns its asset number. Enter company, class, description, serial/tag, quantity, purchase date, supplier/invoice reference, organization assignment, notes, and applicable depreciation method/life/rate/residual/start date. Save the Planned record, then use the appropriate Asset Capitalization flow to recognize its value. Master data entry alone does not capitalize the asset. Details tab Review or maintain editable master details. Once capitalized, company and class are fixed; valuation changes apply from the next depreciation period and require a reason. The Location where the asset is kept, from Organizational Units is not part of the books and can be changed here at any time, even after depreciation; the change is kept in History. Do not use Master to change a capitalized asset's other assignments division, branch, cost or profit center . Use the designated Asset Transfer workflow when it is available; if it is not on your menu yet, ask the Fixed Asset administrator about the approved transfer process. Planned records may be deleted; posted/capitalized history is retained. History tab Use History to trace creation, capitalization/additions, take over, scheduled and additional depreciation, CWIP costs/settlement, retirement, reversals, and master data changes. Each event shows its date, linked document/GL reference, cost and accumulated depreciation movement, details, and user/time. Review this before troubleshooting NBV or status. What happens in the books Creating or editing the asset master does not post a journal. It supplies details and depreciation inputs to asset transactions. Capitalization, depreciation, retirement, and CWIP settlement create their own accounting entries and update the asset book balances/history. Rights FAASSET access controls viewing; draft allows creating and changing eligible asset records. A capitalized asset's company and class cannot be changed; certain post capitalization changes require a reason. Company access applies. Questions and mistakes Asset is missing from the list: clear the filters and check company, class, and status. No History tab for a new record: history is available for an existing saved asset; the tab appears when you open an existing record. Cannot edit a field: capitalized assets have controlled fields; use the correct transaction module for movements and enter a reason for supported master changes. Depreciation does not appear: check class kind/method, start date, cost/value, depreciation status, period sequence, and mapped accounts. NBV differs from expectation: compare cost and scheduled/additional accumulated depreciation in Details with the dated transactions in History. Related pages Fixed Asset Configuration fixed asset config.html · Capitalization fixed asset capitalization.html · Depreciation Run depreciation run.html · Fixed Asset Retirement fixed asset retirement.html

pages.title: Fixed Asset Capitalization
pages.summary: Record the purchase or acquisition of a fixed asset and place it into service for depreciation.
pages.text: Fixed Asset Capitalization What it is for Fixed Asset Capitalization brings a purchased or self constructed asset into the ERP’s fixed asset register for depreciation. Before you start The asset master is already created or the class is known. The supplier or vendor invoice or accumulation record is ready. The account mapping is set in Fixed Asset Configuration. Step by step 1. Open Fixed Asset Capitalization . 2. Select the asset or create the asset from the acquisition entry. 3. Enter the acquisition value, date and any related cost details. 4. Post the acquisition. The asset is then available for depreciation. What happens in the books The capitalization posts the asset to the fixed asset register and moves the value from the clearing or purchase account into the asset account. Rights Finance or asset support roles generally need access and post rights for capitalisation. Questions and mistakes If posting is refused, check the class setup, clearing account and asset status.

pages.title: Capital Work in Progress
pages.summary: Track capital work under construction until it is completed and transferred into a fixed asset.
pages.text: Capital Work in Progress What it is for Capital Work in Progress tracks a project or asset under construction before it is fully ready for use. This keeps the asset value segregated until it is ready for capitalization. Before you start The project or asset class is configured. The asset under construction is assigned to an accountable class. The user knows which costs belong in the capital work account. Step by step 1. Open Capital Work in Progress and select the company. 2. Add the work in progress asset or project. 3. Record the values or costs being accumulated. 4. When the asset is ready, transfer it to the final fixed asset record. What happens in the books The balance remains in the capital work in progress account until the asset is transferred into service and capitalized. Rights Finance and asset setup roles generally maintain this area. Questions and mistakes If the transfer is not visible, check that the work in progress asset is active and linked to the correct class.

pages.title: Depreciation Run
pages.summary: Calculate and post the monthly depreciation for the active fixed asset register.
pages.text: Depreciation Run What it is for Depreciation Run has two tabs: Run previews and posts the scheduled charge for one company and month; Depreciation Register reports asset balances over a period range. The run uses each asset's class, method, depreciation start, posting history, and any catch up due. Before you start Assets are capitalized, active, and assigned to a depreciable tangible or intangible class with a start date and Straight Line or Written Down Value method. Fixed Asset Configuration contains valid depreciation expense and accumulated depreciation accounts. Every asset in the run has a cost center for the expense posting. The month is open for Fixed Asset posting. Runs are posted in monthly order without gaps. Step by step Run tab 1. Select the company and month. The screen shows the last posted month and the next month allowed; the first run may start at the chosen period. 2. Select Preview . Review each asset's opening net book value, scheduled charge, catch up, accumulated depreciation, closing net book value, method, and notes. Review totals by class and expense account. 3. Resolve every blocker or asset error before posting. Typical blockers include a period out of sequence, an already posted month, another run still in progress, missing account determination, no cost center, or nothing eligible to depreciate. 4. Select Post Depreciation after reviewing the preview. Posting recalculates the run and writes the asset transactions and GL journal. If posting was interrupted, reopen the same period and use Finish Posting to resume that run. 5. Review the run list and open Lines to inspect a posted or reversed run. Export the preview or lines to CSV when needed. Depreciation Register tab Choose From and To periods, then Show . Review opening NBV, scheduled depreciation, additional depreciation, accumulated depreciation, and closing NBV by asset; use CSV for reconciliation. Reverse a run Only the latest posted period can be reversed. Enter a reason. Reverse any later fixed asset postings on the run's assets first. If the accounting month is closed, the system offers an adjustment in the first open month; confirm that prompt only when that treatment is intended. After reversal, the period can be posted again. What happens in the books The run creates a journal dated on the period's last day: debit depreciation expense, grouped by account and cost center, and credit accumulated depreciation. It also writes a depreciation transaction for each asset, updates the asset's accumulated depreciation and net book value, and marks an asset Fully Depreciated when appropriate. No approval step is required by this screen; the post right controls posting. Rights FADEPRUN access allows viewing runs/registers; post permits posting; reverse permits reversal of the latest run. Company access applies. Questions and mistakes Asset is absent from preview: check active status, tangible/intangible class, depreciation method, start date, remaining net book value, and selected company. Posting is blocked: resolve the account or cost center errors and check that this is the next unposted month. Run says posting is in progress: reopen and post that same period to finish it before starting another. Charge includes catch up: review the period history and depreciation start date; catch up covers eligible depreciation from an earlier period not previously scheduled. Need to reverse a non latest period: reverse later runs first; the process deliberately preserves chronological asset balances. Month is closed: review the offered first open month adjustment before continuing; do not edit the resulting GL journal directly. Related pages Fixed Asset Configuration fixed asset config.html · Fixed Asset Register fixed asset register.html · Additional Depreciation additional depreciation.html · Period Closing period closing.html

pages.title: Additional Depreciation
pages.summary: Add one-off depreciation adjustments for assets with unusual or exceptional value changes.
pages.text: Additional Depreciation What it is for Additional Depreciation is a separate posting document for a justified, one off charge beyond scheduled depreciation, such as damage or a policy directed reduction. It applies only to Active Tangible or Intangible assets and cannot reduce an asset below its residual value. Before you start The asset is Active, depreciable, and has a valid class/account determination and cost center. The posting date is on or after the asset's capitalization/depreciation start and in or after the latest posted depreciation period. The reason, amount, and approval policy are documented; an amount above NBV less residual value is rejected. Step by step 1. Open Additional Depreciation and create a draft. Select company, date, required reason, optional description/reference, and one or more eligible assets. 2. For each asset, compare current NBV and At most with the proposed additional amount. Enter no more than NBV less residual value. 3. Review the total and the displayed GL impact. Save/post the draft. If Approval Configuration is enabled, it becomes Pending Approval; nothing posts until approval. A rejected entry can be corrected and resubmitted. 4. After posting, open the GL entry and asset history to confirm the expense, accumulated depreciation, and new NBV. The scheduled depreciation engine spreads the lower remaining balance over the remaining life. 5. Reverse an incorrect posted entry with a reason. Reversal may be blocked if a later financial transaction exists on the asset; reverse later transactions first. What happens in the books Posting debits the class's Additional Depreciation Expense account or the configured Depreciation Expense fallback and credits Accumulated Depreciation. The asset transaction records the reduction in NBV. The posting is separate from the scheduled Depreciation Run. Rights FAADDDEP access controls viewing; draft creates/edits/deletes Draft or Rejected documents; post submits/posts, approves/rejects when assigned, and reverses. Company access and Approval Configuration apply. Questions and mistakes Asset is not selectable: it must be Active and Tangible or Intangible; Land, AuC, retired, and transferred assets are not eligible. Amount is too high: the maximum is current NBV less residual value as of the posting date. Date is rejected: use a date no earlier than capitalization/depreciation start and no earlier than the latest posted depreciation period; the accounting period must also be open. Expense account missing: configure Additional Depreciation Expense or its allowed Depreciation Expense fallback in Fixed Asset Configuration. Reversal is blocked: reverse later transactions affecting that asset first, then reverse this posting. Related pages Fixed Asset Configuration fixed asset config.html · Fixed Asset Master fixed asset master.html · Depreciation Run depreciation run.html · Approvals approvals.html

pages.title: Asset Register
pages.summary: Review the assets in use, their values and their depreciation status company-wide.
pages.text: Fixed Asset Register What it is for Fixed Asset Register is an as at report reconstructed from asset transactions. It shows asset cost and movements, accumulated depreciation, current period depreciation, net book value NBV , disposal proceeds/gain or loss, and asset status as of the selected date. Before you start Capitalization, additions, depreciation, transfers, retirement, and reversals have been posted for the period being reviewed. Select the correct company and as at date. The report can show historical balances, not only today's balance. Know which filters are needed: asset number, class, description, cost center, status, supplier, capitalized date, or purchase date. Step by step 1. Open Fixed Asset Register , select the company and As at date, then choose Show . 2. Narrow the rows by asset number, class, description, cost center, status, supplier, capitalized from/to, or acquired from/to. 3. Review original cost, additions, transfers, retirements, accumulated depreciation, this period charge, NBV, disposal value, gain/loss, and status. Totals and class summaries follow the filtered rows. 4. Open a row to inspect its dated asset history and linked posting documents. Use CSV for spreadsheet analysis or Print for a review copy. 5. Reconcile unusual balances to Fixed Asset Master history, depreciation runs, capitalization, transfers, and retirement entries before changing any source transaction. What happens in the books The register is read only. It reconstructs balances from posted asset transactions and creates no journal. The GL posting remains in the transaction that changed cost or accumulated depreciation. Rights FAREGISTER access controls report visibility; company access limits the report data. CSV/print are report outputs, not postings. Questions and mistakes Asset missing: check the company, as at date, filters, and whether it existed or was capitalized by that date. NBV is unexpected: compare cost, additions, transfers, retirements, accumulated depreciation, and this period depreciation with the transaction history. Disposal gain/loss differs: inspect disposal proceeds and NBV on the retirement date; do not use today's NBV for a past disposal. Class summary doesn't match the unfiltered report: the summary follows the currently filtered rows; clear filters before comparing company totals. Related pages Fixed Asset Master fixed asset master.html · Depreciation Run depreciation run.html · Fixed Asset Capitalization fixed asset capitalization.html · Fixed Asset Retirement fixed asset retirement.html

pages.title: Fixed Asset Retirement
pages.summary: Retire a fixed asset when it is sold, scrapped or otherwise removed from service.
pages.text: Fixed Asset Retirement What it is for Fixed Asset Retirement records the removal of an asset from the fixed asset register when it is sold, discarded or otherwise disposed of. Before you start The asset is in the register and is active. The retirement date and proceeds are agreed. Any gain or loss account mapping is configured. Step by step 1. Open Fixed Asset Retirement and select the asset. 2. Enter the disposal date, proceeds and reason for retirement. For a sale, when the company has a Tax Configuration tax configuration.html , choose the sale's Tax code ; the totals show the tax by component. 3. Review the asset’s net book value and gain or loss on disposal. 4. Post the retirement and verify the asset is closed off correctly. What happens in the books The retirement removes the asset from service and posts the net book value and any gain or loss to the relevant accounts. A sale's tax is worked out from its tax code at the rate on the retirement date. Under India GST it is CGST + SGST when the buyer is in the company's state, or the sale is to the bank, and IGST when a customer is in another state. Each component is credited to its output account, and the receipt bank or customer carries the proceeds plus the tax. Rights Finance and asset support roles normally handle retirement posting. Questions and mistakes Choose the sale's tax code: a company with a Tax Configuration needs one on every sale. If the asset does not retire, confirm the asset is still active and the disposal date is in an open period.

pages.title: Job Order Request
pages.summary: Open a job order request to start production and confirm the required materials and output.
pages.text: Job Order Request What it is for Job Order Request records a manufacturing or production request before the production is released. It defines what is to be made, by when and in what quantity. Before you start The bill of materials and work centres are known. The production date and output target are agreed. The company’s production rules are active. Step by step 1. Open Job Order Request and select the company. 2. Enter the production item, quantity and required date. 3. Confirm the materials or cost basis associated with the job. 4. Submit or approve the request and move it into production. What happens in the books The job order request is a planning record. The actual production posting and consumption entries happen later when the job is processed. Rights Production planners and maintenance or admin users with job order access usually use this screen. Questions and mistakes If the job is not created, check whether the item and production setup are active.

pages.title: Bill of Materials
pages.summary: Define what a finished product is made of and how the materials are consumed during production.
pages.text: Bill of Materials What it is for Bill of Materials BOM is the dated production recipe for a Finished Good or Semi Finished Good. It records the components and required quantities for one unit of the parent item; Material Variance uses the BOM version effective on each production date. Before you start The parent item exists in Item Master as a Finished Good or Semi Finished Good. Each component exists as a Raw Material, Semi Finished Good, or Consumable and has a base unit of measure. The recipe version, effective date, component quantities per one parent unit, and expected scrap percentages have been approved by production. Step by step 1. Open BOM and search/filter the list by parent item or status. Select New BOM , or open an existing record and choose Duplicate to create a new version from it. 2. Select the parent Finished or Semi Finished Good, enter the recipe version and Effective From date, and add notes if needed. 3. Add eligible component items. Enter quantity per one unit of the parent in the component's base UOM, plus Scrap % where applicable. Paste rows from Excel using Component Code, Quantity, and Scrap %; review the resulting UOM and quantities. 4. Save the BOM. When a BOM is marked Active, another Active BOM for the same parent is automatically deactivated. Effective dates still matter: historical reports select the recipe that applied on the transaction date, not simply today's active row. 5. Deactivate or reactivate a recipe from the list when its use changes. Keep prior versions for historical production and variance analysis; do not rewrite an old recipe to represent a later change. What happens in the books Saving a BOM creates no stock or GL posting. Production uses the recipe to calculate expected components and finished output; the BOM's effective date also determines expected component usage in Material Variance reports. Rights The BOM access right controls viewing; write rights control creating, editing, duplicating, and changing status. Follow the business's production maintenance controls when granting write access. Questions and mistakes Parent item is missing: only active Finished Goods and Semi Finished Goods can be parents; create or correct the item in Item Master first. Component is missing: use Raw Material, Semi Finished Good, or Consumable items. Check the item's base UOM and active status. Historical variance uses a different recipe: check Effective From dates; a report for an earlier production date uses the version effective then. Another version became inactive: only one BOM per parent can be Active at a time. The prior version remains available for history; confirm the new effective date is correct. Production standard quantity looks wrong: quantity is per one parent unit, in the component's base UOM; verify quantity and Scrap % before saving. Related pages Item Master item master.html · Production production.html · Production & Consumption production consumption.html · Material Variance material variance.html

pages.title: Production Entry
pages.summary: Record produced output into stock and post its assigned inventory/consumption accounting; component issue remains separate.
pages.text: Production Entry What it is for Production Entry records finished output entering stock. It can optionally link to a submitted Job Order batch so produced quantities fulfil its matching lines. It does not consume BOM components; record actual component issues separately in Material Issue. Before you start The output item, warehouse, positive quantity, unit cost, and applicable batch/expiry information are confirmed. Item Master has a valid Consumption account; the item and UOM are active and belong to the selected company. If linking a Job Order, the batch is Submitted, belongs to the same company, and its matching line is eligible for production progress. The posting date is open and Production approval is configured if required. Step by step 1. Open Production Entry and create a document. Choose company, date, description, optional reference, dimensions, and optional submitted Job Order batch. 2. Add each produced item, warehouse, description, UOM, quantity, positive unit cost, batch/expiry when relevant, and cost/profit center. The cost can be entered or populated from the effective production unit cost list. 3. Review line totals and output quantities. Check that the Job Order is still Submitted and has eligible lines for the output item; at posting the system matches by item code and updates the corresponding line progress. 4. Save as Draft and post. If approval is configured, the entry remains pending and stock/GL/job progress do not change until final approval. A rejected entry is editable and can be resubmitted. 5. After posting, check the finished item's warehouse balance, GL Impact, Job Order progress if linked, and any Sales Order shortfalls allocated from newly available stock. Reverse with a reason if the output entry is wrong. What happens in the books Each production line posts an inbound stock movement at its entered unit cost and a GL journal: debit inventory and credit the item's Consumption account. The line quantity/value are stored for stock reports. Components are not relieved from the BOM automatically; Material Issue posts their actual consumption separately. Reversal cancels the output and corresponding GL impact. Rights PRODUCTION access controls viewing; draft creates/edits/deletes Draft or Rejected entries; post submits/posts, approves/rejects where assigned, and reverses. Company access applies. Questions and mistakes Expected components were not deducted: Production records output only. Enter actual component use in Material Issue. A posted entry's Job Order shows "no longer open for production": its lines are complete often by this very entry . It stays linked; it is only no longer offered for new entries. Job Order progress did not update: check the selected batch and eligible matching item lines; progress updates only after the production commit succeeds. Cost/account error: use a positive unit cost, verify the item's Consumption account, and ensure the inventory account is configured. Batch tracked output rejected: enter a batch number and valid expiry where the item requires it. Approval is pending: no stock, GL, Job Order progress, or order allocation changes until approved. Output does not appear in availability: check company, warehouse, posted status, and any later reversal. Related pages Bill of Materials bill of materials.html · Material Issue material issue.html · Job Order Request job order request.html · Inventory Valuation List inventory valuation.html · Material Variance material variance.html

pages.title: Production & Consumption Report
pages.summary: Report posted production output or net material consumption by date, category, and sub-category.
pages.text: Production & Consumption Report What it is for Production & Consumption Report has two report modes: Production totals finished output, while Consumption totals net component usage. Despite the module name, this screen does not enter or post material consumption; use Production and the stock movement documents to record activity. Before you start Production entries and stock movements for the selected period are posted. Item category/sub category setup is correct if those filters will be used. The user has Production & Consumption report access for the selected company. Step by step 1. Open Production & Consumption Report and select either Production or Consumption . 2. Choose the company, date range, and optional item Category and Sub Category filters. 3. Run the report. Review quantity and value by item, grouped with subtotals by category/sub category and a grand total. 4. Copy the table to Excel or print it for a period review. Use Material Variance material variance.html when the question is expected BOM consumption versus actual consumption. 5. If a movement is wrong or missing, correct the source Production, Material Issue, Stock Adjustment, or Physical Count document; rerunning this report only rereads posted transactions. What happens in the books This is a read only report and does not change stock or post a journal. Production mode reports posted output; Consumption mode nets Material Issue, Stock Adjustment, and Physical Count movements, including reversals, for the date range. Rights The Production & Consumption Report access right controls viewing. Posting rights belong to the source Production and inventory modules, not this report. Questions and mistakes Consumption total differs from Material Issue: Stock Adjustment and Physical Count movements are included too; check the net quantity for each item and date range. Production and consumption do not reconcile: production output and component consumption are separate movement types; use Material Variance for BOM standard versus actual usage. Sub Category filter is empty: add and activate sub categories under the item's fixed parent category, then assign them in Item Master. Report is empty: confirm the company/date range and that source transactions are Posted, not Draft, pending, or rejected. Related pages Production production.html · Material Issue material issue.html · Stock Adjustment stock adjustment.html · Physical Count physical count.html · Material Variance material variance.html

pages.title: Material Variance Report
pages.summary: Compare BOM-expected component use with net actual stock consumption for production in a date range.
pages.text: Material Variance Report What it is for Material Variance Report compares the BOM quantity expected for production with actual stock consumption over a date range. It is a read only analysis report, not a transaction for entering or posting a variance. Expected usage is based on the BOM version effective on each production date. Actual usage nets Material Issue, Stock Adjustment, and Physical Count movements, so it can differ from the total on Material Issue alone. Before you start Production and related stock movements for the period are posted. BOM versions and effective dates are correct for the production dates being analyzed. The user can access the selected company and has Material Variance Report access. Step by step 1. Open Material Variance Report and select the company and From/To dates. 2. Run the report. Review the items produced during the range first; this is the output population used in the comparison. 3. For each component, compare Expected BOM , Actual, Variance, and Variance %. A positive variance means actual consumption is higher than expected; a negative variance means it is lower. 4. Check the warning on any produced item with no BOM effective on its production date. Its output is listed, but it is not included in expected component consumption. 5. Copy the result table to a spreadsheet for investigation or use Print for a review copy. Trace an unexpected figure to the BOM version, production posting, and material movements in the same date range. What happens in the books Running, copying, or printing the report does not change inventory, production documents, or the general ledger. The report explains quantity differences; correct the underlying BOM, production, issue, stock adjustment, or count document through its own module. It does not create a variance journal. Rights The Material Variance Report's access right controls the report. It is separate from the rights to create Production, Material Issue, Stock Adjustment, or Physical Count documents. Questions and mistakes No rows appear: check the company and date range, and confirm production or component stock movement was posted in that period. Expected quantity is missing: check that the item had an active BOM on the production date. A BOM created later does not retroactively define earlier production. Actual differs from Material Issue totals: the report also nets relevant Stock Adjustment and Physical Count movements, and reversal movements cancel their originals. Variance looks doubled after a reversal: verify both the original production and its reversal are posted; a reversal should cancel the original output and expected usage. A large positive or negative amount: drill into production quantities, the effective BOM component quantities, and all stock movements for that material before changing a source record. Related pages Production production.html · Bill of Materials bill of materials.html · Material Issue material issue.html · Stock Adjustment stock adjustment.html · Physical Count physical count.html

pages.title: Company Master
pages.summary: Keep the company profile, chart links and the legal defaults used across the ERP.
pages.text: Company Master Data What it is for Company Master holds the company profile and many of the legal and operational defaults that the rest of the ERP relies on, including account structure and tax related settings. Before you start The legal company information is agreed. The financial account and tax configuration is ready. The business knows which setup defaults must be shared across all modules. Step by step 1. Open Company Master and select the company. Companies are listed in code order 01, 02 … 10 . 2. Review the company information and operational defaults. 3. Set the required account links and the fields that should be shared with all modules. 4. Save and test a standard transaction against the company setup. Shareholders Select Shareholders the people icon on a company to see and keep its shareholders: name, nationality, ID or passport number, shares held, and the dates they held them from and to. Enter the company's Issued shares : each shareholder's % is worked out of them. If the current shareholders don't hold exactly the issued shares 100% , a warning says so; you can still save, for example while a transfer is being entered. A shareholder who sold or left: edit them and enter the To date. They stay on the list as a past shareholder, so the history is kept. A record entered by mistake can be removed, with a reason. Changes lists every change: who made it and when. Print company profile prints the company's details with its current shareholders and their %. What happens in the books Company Master is a setup record and not a posting document by itself. It provides the default company rules used by many other screens. Rights Usually restricted to ERP admin or finance support roles. Shareholders are personal data, so they have their own right: Company Master shareholders in Roles & Permissions, to see them. Changing them also needs Company Master's write right. Questions and mistakes If a screen cannot find the company or accounts, the company profile may not be set correctly.

pages.title: Organizational Units
pages.summary: Maintain divisions, branches, warehouses, racks, cost centers, profit centers, locations and projects used by ERP workflows.
pages.text: Organizational Units What it is for Organizational Units maintains reusable operating and reporting dimensions: Divisions, Branches, Warehouses, Racks, Cost Centers, Profit Centers, and Locations. A Location is where people work and assets are kept an office, a site, a yard : it is chosen on the employee record and on the fixed asset record, and does not post to the books. A Cost Center is commonly used as the department for employee/payroll assignment, but there is no separate Department unit type. A Project is a job you want to see the result of a building, a contract . It can name its Customer and its Start and End dates. Journal, cash and bank lines and invoices carry it, and the Project Report project report.html shows its income, costs and result. A project is Active or Closed : a closed project takes no new postings, though an entry on it can still be reversed. Units can be shared across companies or restricted to one company. Parent links build a hierarchy; Racks are the exception with a required Warehouse parent. Before you start The unit codes, names, types, parent relationships, and company ownership are agreed. Company specific units are assigned to a company; leave Company blank only when the unit is intentionally shared. Reporting, approval, employee, warehouse, and asset owners agree which dimensions they will select. Step by step 1. Open Organizational Units . Search by code/name and use the type or status filter to review existing units. 2. Add an item and choose its type, unique code, name, optional parent, company scope, and Active status. 3. For a Rack, select a Warehouse as its parent. Other unit types may be arranged under an appropriate parent; do not create a parent cycle. 4. Save, then confirm the unit appears in the correct type specific picker. Check company scope before assigning a warehouse or employee dimension. 5. Edit a unit to correct its details. Deactivate rather than delete a unit that should no longer be selected. Reassign/deactivate active child units before deactivating their parent. Rights ORGUNITS access allows viewing; write allows creating, editing, deactivating, and reactivating units. Company access is checked when assigning a company specific unit. Questions and mistakes Unit missing from a picker: check its type, Active status, company scope, and the module's company access. Rack cannot be saved: it must have an existing Warehouse parent. "Only a project is Closed" : other units are Active or Inactive. "… is closed: it takes no new postings" on an entry: the project was closed; reopen it Active or choose another. Parent cannot be deactivated: first deactivate or reassign all active child units. Parent relationship is refused: the parent must exist, cannot be the unit itself, and cannot be one of its descendants. Code is rejected as duplicate: codes are unique across the Organizational Units list, not only within a single type. Company specific warehouse is not available: the unit is restricted to its company; confirm the user and transaction are operating in that company. Organizational Units do not post to the general ledger. They supply dimensions and locations used by other modules. Related pages Company Master company master.html · HR Setup hr setup.html · Employee Master employees.html · Approvals approvals.html

pages.title: User Management
pages.summary: Set up ERP users, assign roles and control which screens they can access and post.
pages.text: User Management What it is for User Management maintains ERP login accounts and their profile: username, name, email, role, Active/Inactive status, and assigned companies. The role determines module capabilities; company assignment limits which company data the user can access. Before you start The user's identity, username, email, role, account status, and company assignments are confirmed. Roles and their module rights are configured in Roles & Permissions roles.html . Assign only the companies the user needs. Leaving Assigned Companies empty denies access to company scoped finance and reporting data. Step by step 1. Open User Management and search/filter by username, email/name, role, or Active/Inactive status. A user linked to an employee who is leaving shows Leaving: access until a date under the status, or Access ended once it has passed: from then on they can't sign in. The date is set from the employee record Employees , where HR can extend it. Last Login shows when each user last signed in, in your local time. Never means they have not signed in since the column started being recorded October 2026 . Reopening the ERP in a tab where you are still signed in does not count as a new sign in. 2. To add a user, click Add New User and enter username, email, full name, role, status, password minimum six characters , and one or more assigned companies. Review the company list carefully before saving. The username is also the user's user ID for signing in, so no two users may share it capitals don't count: "Kim" and "kim" are the same . 3. To edit a user, update full name, role, status, and company assignments. Username/email are not edited from the existing user form; coordinate account identity changes through the approved identity process. 4. Test access using the assigned role and company. Menu visibility comes from Tree Management, while actual read/draft/post capabilities come from Roles & Permissions. 5. To remove ERP access, use Remove Access. This removes the ERP profile/access; it does not delete the user's Firebase Authentication account. What happens in the books User Management does not post accounting entries. It controls login/profile data; role capabilities, company assignment, and menu visibility are enforced separately by the ERP. Rights USERMGMT access/write rights control user administration. Limit these rights to trusted administrators. Changing someone's role or company assignment can immediately change their data visibility and available actions. Questions and mistakes User sees no menu item: check the role's visibility on the node and all menu ancestors in Tree Management. Menu appears but access is denied: check the module capability and company assignment in Roles & Permissions/User Management. User has no company data: assign the needed company; an empty assignment does not provide company scoped finance/report access. User cannot be edited: the username is fixed on the existing user form; use the approved identity management process rather than creating a duplicate casually. Remove Access did not disable Google sign in: the Firebase Auth account remains; the ERP profile/access is what this action removes. Related pages Roles & Permissions roles.html · Tree Management tree management.html · Company Master company master.html

pages.title: Roles and Permissions
pages.summary: Define which roles can open, edit, approve, post or report on each module.
pages.text: Roles & Permissions What it is for Roles & Permissions has two connected parts: a list of roles, and a module capability matrix. Users receive one role in User Management; the matrix controls what that role can do in each module. Company assignment and menu visibility are separate controls. Before you start Define role responsibilities and least privilege capabilities before changing the matrix. Create the required roles before assigning them to users in User Management user management.html . Review the actual capability names for each module; they vary by workflow for example access, draft, post, pay, report, return, or sensitive . The matrix lists the modules your organisation has. Rights you gave for a module it no longer has are kept, and apply again if it has it back. Step by step Maintain roles 1. Add a role with a unique name and a brief description of its purpose, or edit the existing role. 2. Delete a role only when no user currently has it and another role retains the required administrative write access. Default favourites The star on a role's row sets up to 5 screens to show at the top of the menu for users of that role. It applies only to users who haven't chosen favourites of their own, and only to screens the user may open. Once a user changes their favourites user menu → Configure Favourites , the list is theirs, and later changes to the role's defaults leave it alone. The row shows how many defaults the role has. Maintain module capabilities 1. In Module Permissions , read across each module/capability row and role column. A checked box grants that capability to that role. 2. Grant only the actions needed for the role: viewing is different from drafting, submitting/posting, paying, reporting, returning, or viewing sensitive data. 3. Save the matrix once after reviewing the full set of changes. The system prevents removing the last role's write access to Roles & Permissions or User Management. 4. Test with a representative user assigned to the role: confirm both allowed actions and actions that should be denied. Menu visibility is not a permission grant. Configure the navigation separately in Tree Management tree management.html , and assign companies separately in User Management user management.html . What happens in the books Role and permission changes do not post accounting entries. They change which callable actions the server permits for users assigned to those roles. Rights ROLES write access controls role and permission administration. At least one role must retain write access to both Roles & Permissions and User Management to avoid locking out administrators. Questions and mistakes User can see a menu item but cannot open/use it: check the module capability and company assignment; tree visibility alone is not enough. User cannot see the module in navigation: check Tree Management role visibility separately from module capabilities. Capability is absent from the matrix: capabilities are module specific; use the exact available capability rather than assuming every module has generic read/write/post rights. Role cannot be deleted: reassign its users first; the last administrative role cannot be removed if it is the only one retaining required write access. A permission change did not affect an already open screen: have the user refresh/reopen the module and test the current role assignment. Related pages User Management user management.html · Tree Management tree management.html · Approval Configuration approval configuration.html

pages.title: Tree Management
pages.summary: Build the menu tree and link each module to the right company, role and section.
pages.text: Module Tree & Navigation What it is for Tree Management builds the hierarchical navigation menu. Each node has display text, a parent, an optional linked module, an order, and a list of roles allowed to see it. A reference node can organize the menu without opening a screen. Before you start The intended menu hierarchy and labels are agreed. Modules are registered and their permissions are configured in Roles & Permissions. Identify which roles should see each menu node. Menu visibility does not itself grant a module capability. The modules offered are the ones your organisation has. A module it does not have is left out of the menu, even if a node still links it. Step by step 1. Open Tree Management and review the existing hierarchy. Add a top level item or add a child beneath the intended parent. 2. Set the node text, optional parent, optional linked module, and allowed roles. Use a node without a linked module for a heading/reference item. An item either opens a module or holds sub items, never both: the ERP refuses a module on an item that has sub items, and a sub item under an item that opens a module. A top level item is an area of the menu: it never opens a module, whether you save it there or drag it there. 3. Drag a node above or below another node to reorder it; dropping on another node can also move it under that node's parent. Save the move and confirm the final hierarchy. 4. Edit the node if its label, parent, module link, or allowed roles change. Check parent visibility: a child is visible only when it and every ancestor allow the user's role. 5. Delete a node only after its child nodes are removed or reassigned. Test the menu as representative roles after any structural change. What happens in the books Tree changes update navigation configuration only; they do not post to the ledger or grant accounting rights. Module actions are still controlled independently by Roles & Permissions and company assignment. Rights TREEMGMT access/write rights control who can view and edit the menu tree. Restrict changes to administrative users; role checkboxes control visibility, not permission to post data. Questions and mistakes Node is visible but screen access is denied: configure the module's access capability separately in Roles & Permissions. Child is missing for a role: check the Allowed Roles on the node and every ancestor. Node appears but opens no module: it may be a reference node with no linked module; edit the module link if it should launch a screen. Cannot move/delete a node: ensure it is not being placed under itself/its descendant and remove or reassign its children first. Related pages Roles and Permissions roles.html · User Management user management.html · Getting Started getting started.html

pages.title: Approval Configuration
pages.summary: Set the approval rules by module, level and company so documents flow to the right approvers.
pages.text: Approval Configuration What it is for Approval Configuration controls transaction approvals by module, scope, and amount. It also configures follow up teams for selected workflows. Approval is not enabled merely because a module has levels: both the module setting and applicable saved levels determine whether a document is gated. Before you start The business has agreed which document types need approval, the amount thresholds, approval scopes, and named approvers. Users, company assignments, and organizational units are configured and active. The relevant module is available and its documents identify the scope and amount used by the approval check. Step by step Configure approval 1. Open Approval Configuration and choose the module/document type from the list. 2. Set Enabled , choose a scope, and choose the gate type: Global uses one rule for the whole system. Company , Division , Branch , or Cost Center stores separate rules at that scope. Threshold applies a level when the document amount is at or above that level's threshold. Every qualifying level is required. Two levels with the same threshold, such as zero, are both required for every amount. Flat is a required approval without amount thresholds. 3. Select the scope record skip this picker for Global . Add one or more levels and assign the specific approver user for each. Save the module settings and level records. 4. Configure the required scope values consistently. A Company scoped module needs levels saved for each company that should use approval; changing the scope type does not create the levels for you. 5. For a module with a Follow up Team panel, select the users for that scope and save separately. Follow up tasks are not approval levels: everyone selected receives the Home task, and the first person to act clears it for the group. The teams are: Production Sales Job Orders and Procurement Purchase and Inventory Purchase Requisitions ; Invoicing Delivery Note : a posted delivery stays in the team's tasks until a posted customer invoice includes it; with no team for its scope, the user who made the delivery gets the task; Treasury PDC Received and PDC Issued : a pending cheque appears in the team's Home tasks a number of days before its date Days before the cheque date , 3 to start, one setting for every company and both screens . Once a team is set for a scope, only the team sees those cheques; with no team, everyone who may post PDCs sees them from the cheque date. 6. Test with a draft transaction below and above the intended threshold, and confirm the right approver sees the task. Also test the no approval case if some scopes intentionally have no levels. What happens in the books Configuration changes do not post to the general ledger. When a transaction is submitted, the module resolves its scope and amount, snapshots the required levels into an approval instance, and waits for every applicable approval. The transaction module performs the posting only after its own approval rules are satisfied. A module enabled with no applicable levels is not gated. Rights APPROVALCONFIG access/write rights control viewing and maintaining configuration. The named approvers need the relevant module/document access and company scope to review their tasks. Follow up team members need access to the relevant task workflow; assigning a person here does not grant module rights. Questions and mistakes Document bypasses approval: confirm Enabled is on and levels exist for the document's actual scope key. Enabled without levels does not gate. More people are required than expected: each level whose threshold is at or below the document amount applies; repeated thresholds make levels apply together. No level applies: check the document amount, threshold values, scope type, and whether levels were saved for the selected company/unit. Approver cannot act: confirm the level names that exact active user, and that they can access the document's module and company. Follow up users do not see tasks: confirm the module supports a follow up team, the correct scope's team was saved, and the selected users can access the workflow. Follow up is separate from approval. Approval setting appears to change an in flight document: already submitted documents use the approval instance captured at submission; test configuration with a new draft. Related pages Approval Tracker approval tracker.html · Approvals approvals.html · Roles and Permissions roles.html · Organisation Units org units.html

pages.title: Approval Tracker
pages.summary: Track each approval request, see who acted and follow the current status of a document.
pages.text: Approval Tracker What it is for Approval Tracker is an audit view of approval instances across gated modules. It shows one row per required approval level, including levels still Pending, the assigned approver, decision/reason, self approval flag, and time taken from initial submission. Before you start An approval instance exists for the document; ungated documents do not appear as approval activity. The user has Approval Tracker access and, if delegating, the relevant delegation right. The document number, module, approver, and date range are known for narrowing the register. Step by step 1. Open Approval Tracker. Filter by module, document number, approver, status Pending, Approved or Rejected , and submitted date range. 2. Review each level's Decision: Pending, Approved, or Rejected. Pending time is calculated live from the instance creation time; completed time is measured from the original submission, not from the prior level. 3. Inspect the rejection/approval reason, self approved indicator, and any current delegation note. Copy the filtered rows to Excel for audit follow up. 4. If the user is authorized, select Delegate on a pending level to assign that one level to another user with a reason. Admins may also delegate all pending levels of an absent approver; an approver may delegate their own pending levels. 5. Verify the delegate and reason in the tracker. A delegation changes who can act on the pending level; it does not change the approval threshold or approve the document. 6. An Admin can Close a rejected document that will not be submitted again: it leaves its submitter's tasks, and its row shows "Closed, not resubmitted" and who closed it. The rejection and its reason stay on record. What happens in the books The tracker is read only apart from delegation and closing a rejection. It does not post journals or change the underlying transaction. The originating module posts only when its approval workflow reaches the required final state. Rights APPROVALTRACKER access controls viewing. Delegation rights are separate: approvers can delegate their own pending approvals; Admin can delegate another approver's pending work. Access to the underlying document remains controlled by its module and company permissions. Questions and mistakes A document is missing: check that its module approval was enabled and applicable levels existed when it was submitted; the tracker records approval instances, not all transactions. The pending approver is unexpected: compare the document's amount and scope with Approval Configuration and check any delegation shown. Time Taken looks longer than the previous level: duration is from initial submission, so each level's clock overlaps. Cannot delegate: only pending levels can be delegated; check whether the current user may delegate that approver/level and whether the delegate is active. A document is approved but not posted: approval tracking ends at the decision; the source module may still require a separate post or payment action. Related pages Approval Configuration approval configuration.html · Approvals approvals.html · User Management user management.html

pages.title: Numbering
pages.summary: Maintain the document prefixes, numbering format and automatic code generation across modules.
pages.text: Numbering What it is for Numbering customizes the formats for document numbers and master codes. It groups numbered types by category, shows each current format and a sample, and records format changes in a log. Account codes and audit references such as TXN , STK , and PRL are not configured here. Before you start The owner has approved the prefix, company code inclusion, year, separator, sequence width, and order for the affected type. Check the current/default format and existing numbering before changing it; a format change affects new numbers only. Users can access Numbering; only users with the write right can save a format. Step by step 1. Open Numbering and search by type name or prefix. The table groups document numbers, master codes, and HR documents and shows a sample for company 01/current year. Each item category of your own added in Item Master item master.html has its own row under master codes, like the five. The Proforma Invoice PI series numbers the proformas printed from a Sales Order sales order.html proforma invoice . Under HR documents, Employee Request RQ numbers the requests of the types HR sets up in Employee Requests employee requests.html request types . A sales rep's receipts are not here: each rep numbers their own, RC <rep code 000001 see Sales reps sales rep portal.html . 2. Select Edit for the exact type. Set the prefix 1–10 letters/digits , running number width 3–10 digits , optional 2 or 4 digit year, optional company code, separator dash, slash, or none , and year/company order where applicable. 3. Review the live sample. A year in the format creates a separate sequence per year; omitting the company code shares a sequence across companies. Company code formats are unavailable for master types that do not belong to one company. 4. Save. The change is logged and applies only to numbers generated afterwards; existing documents and codes are not renamed. 5. Use Reset to default only when the old system format is intended. Reset restores the default format but does not reset the counter; new numbers continue from the existing counter. What happens in the books Numbering configuration creates no journal and does not change existing records.
