At document creation, the selected format combines prefix, optional company/year, separator, and a zero padded running counter. Customized formats are checked against other types to prevent overlapping number shapes; issued custom numbers are not reused. Rights NUMBERING access controls viewing formats and the change log; write permits editing/resetting formats. Use a tightly restricted administrative role because changes affect all subsequent documents of that type. Questions and mistakes Existing numbers did not change: expected; Numbering is prospective, not a renumbering tool. Sequence did not restart: the format needs a year component for a separate annual sequence. Companies share one sequence: include the company code to scope the number by company, if the type supports it. Format is rejected as a duplicate: change the prefix or other parts so it cannot match another type's current, default, or previously used shape. Reset did not start at 1: reset restores the default format but retains its existing counter. Account code or TXN /STK /PRL reference is unchanged: those are maintained by their owning accounting/audit sequences, not Numbering. Related pages Company Master company master.html · Journal Entries journal entries.html · Master Data Import master import.html

pages.title: Master Data Import
pages.summary: Add or update ERP masters, employee records, opening balances and item barcodes from an Excel paste.
pages.text: Master Data Import What it is for Master Data Import loads many records from a spreadsheet in one checked batch. It covers setup and transaction supporting records across company administration, finance, inventory, procurement, sales, fixed assets, users and HR. It can also update selected existing records, load opening leave and payroll provision balances, and add item barcodes. Full scope In Add new mode, the import list follows this order because later records can depend on earlier ones: 1. Company and organization: Company; Organizational Units. 2. Finance and item setup: Chart of Accounts; Currencies; Unit of Measure UOM ; Item Sub Category; Items. 3. Suppliers and customers: Vendors; Customer Classifications; Customers; Sales Types; Requisition Categories. 4. Fixed assets and inventory: Fixed Asset Classes; Fixed Asset Master; Bill of Materials; Inventory Valuation List; Price Lists. 5. Access and HR: Users; Employees; Leave Opening Balances; Payroll Provision Opening Balances. 6. Item identification: Item Barcodes. Some imports use more than one row for a logical record: use one row per BOM component and one row per price list line. Repeat the BOM or price list details on its rows. A price list import can add lines to an existing list; a new list also needs its currency and any classification mapping. For Employees, active custom fields configured in HR Setup appear as additional columns; Location takes a Location's code or name from Organizational Units. Item Sub Categories have a Company column empty: shared ; an item's sub category is looked for among its company's and the shared ones. Items have an optional User Code column your own code, shown in place of the item code; unique . Employee numbers, item codes, vendor and customer codes, account codes, fixed asset numbers and a company's Ref Code are assigned by the system; do not include them as new record columns. Other references can usually be entered by code or exact name. Update existing is offered for Company, Organizational Units, Chart of Accounts, Currencies, UOM, Items, Vendors, Customers, Fixed Asset Classes, Fixed Asset Master, Users and Employees. Use the record's code as the key Username for Users and Employee No. for Employees . Item Sub Categories, Customer Classifications, Sales Types, Requisition Categories, BOMs, Inventory Valuation Lists, Price Lists, openings and Item Barcodes do not have this update mode. This import does not load GL opening balances, opening stock or vendor/customer open invoices. Those are accounting and stock postings, not master data imports; see Opening Balances opening balances.html . Before you start Prepare a tab separated paste from Excel with the column headers in its first row. Use Copy headers or Copy headers with a sample row to get the exact columns for the selected import. Import prerequisite records first. For example, set up a company's accounts before importing items that refer to them, and set up HR designations and grades before Employees. Check each column's notes and required marker. Use the displayed company code or name, account, item and other reference codes/names as requested. You need access to Master Data Import, the relevant right for the selected module and access to each applicable company. For Users, prepare one temporary password on the screen for the batch. It must be at least six characters; it is not a spreadsheet column or part of the import log. For Update existing , decide which columns to change. The key identifies the record and cannot be changed; only pasted columns are updated. Step by step 1. Open Master Data Import and choose a type from the ordered list. 2. If the type offers Rows , choose Add new or Update existing . In Update mode, use Copy current records to get the key and editable values for records in your companies. 3. Copy the headers and, for a new import, optionally the sample row into Excel. Fill in the rows, then copy the headers and data back into the paste box. 4. Select Check . Review the row and column specific issues below the preview, correct the spreadsheet and check again. No changes are made by Check. 5. Select Import only after the whole batch checks clean, then confirm. Review the result summary, including system generated codes where applicable. Checks and update rules Every row is checked against the same save rules as the corresponding screen, including required fields, references, company access, duplicate names and module specific validation. A reference can use a code or an exact name; where supported, a row can refer by name to a record earlier in the same paste. The paste supports up to 2,000 rows. Headers can be in any order; matching ignores case and spacing. Numbers can include thousands separators. Yes/no fields accept Yes/No, Y/N, True/False or 1/0. Dates accept dd/mm/yyyy also d/m/yyyy, dd mm yyyy and dd.mm.yyyy or yyyy mm dd; impossible dates are rejected. Add new is all or nothing. If any row has an issue, nothing is imported. The import checks again when it runs; if a save fails, records created in that run are undone and the failure is reported. Update existing is also all or nothing. Only pasted columns change. A blank cell keeps its current value; type to clear a value. Compulsory fields cannot be cleared, and locked fields are refused with an explanation. A check preview shows the changes; rows with no changes are skipped. If saving a later row fails, earlier changes in that batch are restored. Every row uses the selected module's own save rules. Update rights are available only for the types listed above and require the relevant edit right. Special cases Users: each imported user receives a sign in using the email in the sheet and the temporary password entered on screen. Usernames and email addresses must be unique. Give each user the password securely and have them change it from the user menu after signing in. Fixed Asset Master: this creates asset records only. Put the asset's value and depreciation into the books through Fixed Asset Capitalization. Bill of Materials: use one row per component. The repeated parent BOM details must agree across all its rows, and an item with an active BOM cannot be overwritten by this import. Inventory Valuation List: only an active Finished Good or Semi Finished Good with an active BOM in the company is eligible. Leave Opening Balances: import one row per employee and balance based leave type. The date is the balance date; entitlement accrues from the following day. Correct an existing opening with an adjustment on the employee's leave card. Payroll Provision Opening Balances: import the employee's provision amount through the date shown. This is a balance already represented in the GL, not a new posting; later payroll runs provide only the change. Tax fields: Items take a Tax Code and HSN / SAC ; Vendors and Customers a Tax Registration Type and State / Emirate a GST state code such as 27, or an emirate code such as DXB , with their City and PIN / Postal Code . A registered party in India's GSTIN is checked against its state, as in the master screens. Item Barcodes: import one row per barcode. A barcode can represent a pack quantity; leave Pack Qty empty for one item unit. Existing barcodes are changed or removed in Item Master. What happens in the books Most imports create or update master/setup records and do not post a finance entry. Leave openings and payroll provision openings establish balances rather than posting them again; Fixed Asset Master creates asset cards but does not capitalize them. GL opening balances, stock openings and open invoices are outside this import. Rights The user needs Master Data Import access and the required capability for the selected master or operation. Company access is checked for the rows being imported. Sensitive employee bank fields require the Employees sensitive right. Questions and mistakes The import type or Update option is missing: check Master Data Import access and the relevant module right. Update mode is not available for every Add new type. A reference is not found or is ambiguous: use its code, or the exact name of a record in the applicable company. Confirm prerequisite records were imported first. Rows have issues: use the row and column shown in the issue list; no rows are saved until the entire batch checks clean. Import reports that nothing was changed: a save failed after checking, for example because the data changed meanwhile. Correct the reported row and run Check again before importing. An opening balance already exists: use the relevant adjustment or balance screen to correct it; opening balances are not updated by import.

pages.title: Document Storage
pages.summary: Store and retrieve supporting files for modules, documents and approvals without going outside the ERP.
pages.text: Document Storage What it is for Document Storage is the Admin setup screen for the private file provider used by supporting document sections throughout the ERP. In production, the ERP connects to Google Drive using an Admin managed OAuth client and refresh token; users open files through the ERP and do not receive direct access to the storage folder. Before you start Admin has created a Google OAuth Web application client and added the exact redirect URI shown by the screen. The connected Drive account is the approved account for business documents and can keep the private ERP Documents folder. Client ID and secret are available to Admin through the approved secure setup process; the secret is stored server side and is not shown again. Step by step 1. Open Document Storage as Admin. Review the connection status and displayed redirect URI. 2. Save the OAuth client ID and secret. Connect Google Drive and sign in as the account that will own/maintain the files; grant the requested access. 3. Use Test connection to confirm the integration can write, read back, and remove a small test file. Refresh the screen to verify connection details. 4. Files are organized under ERP Documents by company, document year, voucher type, and document number. Unnumbered drafts use Drafts and are moved after numbering; removed documents/files are moved to Removed rather than silently erased. 5. If the connection is lost, reconnect the account. Disconnect only when planned: users cannot add/open supporting files until the connection is restored, though existing Drive files remain there. What happens in the books Document Storage configuration and file operations create no journal entries. Files are stored separately from accounting records and linked to their ERP documents through the attachment service. The Drive connection and OAuth credentials are handled server side. Rights Only Admin can open Document Storage and connect/disconnect the provider. Other users add/open supporting files only through the relevant module rights and company access; they do not browse the Drive folder directly. Questions and mistakes Connect button is disabled: save both OAuth client ID and secret first; confirm the redirect URI is registered with Google. Connection test fails: reconnect the approved Drive account and check the OAuth client/consent configuration before users upload more files. A user cannot open a Drive folder: that is expected; files are opened through ERP records, not by granting direct folder access. A document is under Drafts or Removed: draft numbering moves files into their final document folder; removals are retained in the Removed folder for audit. Disconnecting storage: this interrupts all file add/open operations; it does not delete existing files from Drive. Data Reset: clearing Supporting Documents in Data Reset data reset.html moves every file to the Drive's trash kept 30 days , so the storage must be connected at the time. It is the only time the ERP deletes files. Related pages Company Documents company documents.html · Getting Started getting started.html

pages.title: Company Documents
pages.summary: Track company, vendor, customer, and other-party documents, files, renewals, removals, and 30-day expiry reminders.
pages.text: Company Documents What it is for Company Documents is the register for company, vendor, customer, and other party legal records such as licences, contracts, leases, insurance, and tax registrations. It tracks issue/expiry dates, renewal chains, files, category, status, and audit history. Before you start Company Documents access and company access are assigned to the users who maintain or review records. The company, category, title/reference, party if any , issue date, expiry date, and required files are known. Admin has set up the needed document categories. Expiry reminders appear 30 days before expiry and continue after the document expires for users who can maintain the register. Step by step Add or maintain a record 1. Open Company Documents. Search by title/reference/party, and filter by company, category, and status. Current excludes renewed/superseded and removed records; Attention shows expiring or expired records. 2. Add a document with company, category, title, optional reference, optional party, issue/start date, expiry date, and notes. For Vendor or Customer, select the party; for Other, enter the party name. Company documents can have no party. 3. Attach supporting files in the document section. Save and verify the file count/status on the record. 4. Use Terminate for a document no longer in force. Keep the record rather than replacing its history. Renew or remove 1. Open an Active or Terminated document and select Renew . Enter the new record's dates/reference/files and save it. 2. Renewal creates a new version linked to the previous record; the old record becomes Superseded and remains in the version/history chain. Attach the new files to the new version. 3. Use Remove only when the record/files should be removed from normal use. Supply a reason; the record remains as Removed and its stored files move to Removed rather than being silently deleted. Categories Admin can add, rename, or deactivate categories. Deactivating a category prevents it being selected for new documents but leaves it displayed on records that already use it. What happens in the books Company Documents does not post to the ledger. It maintains compliance evidence and expiry reminders. Vendor/customer documents are also visible from their party masters when the user has Company Documents access. Rights COMPANYDOCS access controls viewing; write creates, edits, renews, terminates, and removes records. Only Admin can manage categories. Company access applies. Expiry tasks are sent to users who have both access and write rights. Questions and mistakes Document is not on the current list: it may be Superseded or Removed; change the status filter to find its history. No expiry reminder: check the expiry date, whether it is within 30 days or overdue, and that the user has both access and write rights. Renewal changed the old document: renewal should create a new version and preserve the old one as Superseded; open the version chain to verify. Vendor/customer is unavailable: confirm the party belongs to the selected company or is shared. Category is unavailable: check whether Admin has marked it active; inactive categories remain on existing documents but cannot be newly selected. A file was removed: review the removal reason and storage's Removed area; removal is audited, not an untracked delete. Related pages Document Storage document storage.html · Company Master company master.html · Vendor Master vendor master.html · Customer Master customer master.html

pages.title: Data Reset
pages.summary: Clear test data module by module, or rebuild the stock balances, before going live.
pages.text: Data Reset (Admin) What it is for Data Reset deletes data, for a fresh start while setting up: the test entries made while learning the ERP, or the masters and setup to enter again. It deletes for good: there is no undo. Never use it on live records. It works in your corporate only: a reset never touches another corporate's data. Before you start You are signed in with the ADMIN role: no other role can open it. You know which categories to clear. Nothing is ticked for you. To clear supporting documents, the document storage is connected Document Storage . The categories Transactional data: what accumulates from use. GL entries; stock transactions with the stock balances and reservations; vendor and customer invoices; PDCs; fixed assets; recurring journals; opening balances; Sales Orders; Purchase Requisitions and Orders; Job Orders; approval records; e invoices; employee changes; leave; payroll runs and payslips; final settlements; payroll loans; employee requests; supporting documents; company documents; period closing; the logs. Master data: items and their categories, sub categories, units and barcodes; the chart of accounts; companies; org units; sales types; customer classifications; BOMs; vendors; customers; price lists; the inventory valuation list; requisition categories; currencies and exchange rates; shareholders; employees. Setup: HR Setup, Payroll Setup with the employee request types , Approval Configuration, Tax Configuration, and the numbering formats and settings with the Rep Cash Clearing account . Sales Rep Receipts a transaction are the receipts the reps gave from the Employee Portal; each rep's numbers restart. Their GL entries and cheques are cleared with the GL and PDCs. Users, roles, permissions and the menu are never offered. Step by step 1. Open Data Reset . Each category shows how many records it has. 2. To delete a whole category, tick it. To delete some records only, use Browse & select… on its row where offered . 3. Type DELETE and confirm. What it refuses, and what goes with a category A master still in use is refused. For example, Employees while payroll runs exist, or Customers while invoices exist. The message names what still uses it and how many records it has. Tick those too, or clear them first. Nothing is deleted until the whole selection may go. A master that others use is cleared whole, never one record at a time. Clearing a category restarts its numbering for example, employee numbers or vendor codes . Employees also removes their Employee Portal sign ins, but never an ERP user's own sign in. Supporting Documents also moves the files to the document storage's trash. Google Drive keeps them there for 30 days. A payroll run goes with its payslips, and a Sales Order with its reservations. Recalculate Stock Ledger After deleting single stock transactions, the stock balances may no longer match them. Recalculate Stock Ledger rebuilds the balances from the posted transactions that remain. Rights Only the ADMIN role, whatever Roles & Permissions say. Questions and mistakes "… is still used by …": clear what it names first, or with it. "… not connected": connect the document storage in Document Storage, then clear Supporting Documents again. Deleted the wrong thing: there is no undo. Enter the data again, or restore from your own backup.

pages.title: Support
pages.summary: Send an issue to the ERP's support team, with screenshots or files, and follow their answers.
pages.text: Support What it is for Support is where your Admin tells the ERP's support team about a problem, a question or a change you need, and follows their answers. Only users given Support in Roles by default, Admin see it. What you send is shared. The text and the files go to the support team and are kept in their account, outside your organisation's own. The screen asks you to confirm this every time you send. Send only what the issue needs: one entry's screenshot, not a whole report. Step by step 1. Open Support and select New issue . 2. Choose what it is Bug , Question or Change request , give it a short title for example "The invoice total shows 0" , and pick the screen it is about. 3. Say what you did, what you expected and what you saw instead. Attach up to 5 files of 10 MB each if they help: screenshots, PDF, Word or Excel. 4. Select Send to support and confirm. The issue gets a number, such as 200 00001. 5. Open an issue from the list to read the team's answers. Waiting for you means they need something from you: write your answer with files if needed and Send answer . 6. When it is sorted, the team marks it Resolved . Select Close the issue when you are done with it; for anything more, send a new one. Statuses New: sent, not yet picked up. In progress: the support team is on it. Waiting for you: they asked you something. Resolved: they consider it done; answering reopens it. Closed: finished. It stays in the list to read.
